narrativeReportMd:
# EffectEvidenceSynthesis R4-to-R6 breaking-change assessment

## Bottom line
`EffectEvidenceSynthesis` is a hard breaking removal from the R6 core resource set. R4 instances with `resourceType: "EffectEvidenceSynthesis"` have no same-name R6 StructureDefinition and need conversion to the broader R6 `Evidence` model or another implementation-specific representation.

## Scope
The assigned R6 StructureDefinition path is absent. I searched the R6 package index and old-type CodeSystem and found `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` only as an old FHIR type. The closest R6 core replacement is `Evidence`, which now carries variable definitions, statistics, and certainty. This report treats that as a likely merge target while keeping the findings scoped to local EffectEvidenceSynthesis content.

## Main migration themes
Migration is model redesign rather than field renaming. The R4 resource had mandatory `population`, `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, and `outcome` references, plus local `sampleSize`, `resultsByExposure`, `effectEstimate`, and `certainty` backbones. R6 `Evidence` represents these concepts through repeated `variableDefinition`, `statistic`, `attributeEstimate`, and `certainty` structures with different cardinalities, datatypes, reference targets, and bindings.

## Highest-impact findings
The resource identity removal is critical because strict R6 validators and generated SDKs will reject the R4 resource type. The next highest risks are non-lossless conversion of the variable model and statistical/effect-estimate model. In particular, R4 `resultsByExposure.riskEvidenceSynthesis` points to `RiskEvidenceSynthesis`, which is also listed as an old R6 type rather than an R6 core resource.

## Findings requiring human review
Human review is needed for the conversion rules. The package evidence is strong that the same-name artifact is removed and that `Evidence` is the likely replacement, but the local inputs do not include an official ConceptMap, cross-version extension package, or narrative migration guidance.

## Backward-compatible design observations
Because R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` was low-maturity, consolidation into a broader Evidence model may be justified. A less disruptive approach would have retained deprecated compatibility StructureDefinitions or published a formal map from the R4 resource and its local backbones to R6 `Evidence`.

summary.executiveSummaryMd: `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` is removed from R6 core and appears merged into the broader `Evidence` resource, creating a hard resource-type break. The main migration concerns are replacing the resource identity, remapping mandatory population/exposure/comparator/outcome references into `Evidence.variableDefinition`, and converting effect estimates/results-by-exposure into R6 `Evidence.statistic` structures. The biggest uncertainty is the absence of an official conversion map.
summary.migrationThemesMd: Treat migration as an explicit transform from a narrow effect-synthesis resource into R6 `Evidence`. Preserve old canonical URLs and identifiers where possible, create role-coded variable definitions for population, exposure, comparator, and outcome, map point estimates and precision estimates into `Evidence.statistic.quantity` and `attributeEstimate`, and decide how to preserve `resultsByExposure` links to removed `RiskEvidenceSynthesis` resources. Reverse conversion from R6 Evidence to R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis is often lossy because R6 supports covariates, Group references, observed/intended distinctions, richer statistic attributes, model characteristics, and broader relationship targets.
summary.confidenceSummaryMd: Confidence is high for the resource removal: the R6 same-name file is absent, the R6 package index has no exact StructureDefinition match, and `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` lists `EffectEvidenceSynthesis`. Confidence is medium for detailed field mapping because the local package lacks official diffs, ConceptMaps, narrative migration notes, and several external terminology value set expansions.

findings.title: EffectEvidenceSynthesis is absent from R6 core and appears merged into Evidence

oldState.summary: R4 defines EffectEvidenceSynthesis as a concrete resource.

semanticText.short: A quantified estimate of effect based on a body of evidence
semanticText.definition: The EffectEvidenceSynthesis resource describes the difference in an outcome between exposures states in a population where the effect estimate is derived from a combination of research studies.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 has a concrete `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` StructureDefinition with canonical URL `http://hl7.org/fhir/StructureDefinition/EffectEvidenceSynthesis`, `kind: resource`, `type: EffectEvidenceSynthesis`, and base `DomainResource`.

newState.summary: R6 has no EffectEvidenceSynthesis StructureDefinition; Evidence is the closest replacement.

semanticText.definition: The Evidence Resource provides a machine-interpretable expression of an evidence concept including the evidence variables, the statistics, and the certainty of this evidence.

newState.narrativeMd: The R6 package has no `StructureDefinition-EffectEvidenceSynthesis.json` and no package-index StructureDefinition with id/type/url `EffectEvidenceSynthesis`. R6 `CodeSystem-fhir-old-types` includes `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` as an old type, while R6 `Evidence` now covers variables, statistics, and certainty.

facts.note: The CodeSystem description is: An old resource name no longer used in this version of FHIR (deleted or renamed).
R6 Evidence includes evidence variables, statistics, and certainty.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: A same-name resource was not found. The local R6 evidence-related StructureDefinitions are `Evidence` and `EvidenceVariable`; the R6 `Evidence` definition subsumes the main concepts represented locally in R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis`, so this is best classified as a merge/replacement rather than a narrow rename.

impact.impactRationaleMd: This is a direct resource-level validation and runtime break. An R4 JSON/XML instance with `resourceType: "EffectEvidenceSynthesis"` has no R6 core StructureDefinition, so strict R6 validators, generated model classes, schema generators, REST resource dispatch, and switch statements over resource types will reject or ignore it unless they include an explicit R4 compatibility path. In the reverse direction, a valid R6 `Evidence` instance cannot be assumed to be an R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` because R6 `Evidence` is broader and lacks the old resource identity.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Effect estimates can influence evidence-based recommendations, guideline logic, and clinical decision support. Dropping or misclassifying the resource can lose the distinction between exposure, comparator, outcome, and effect size.

justification.inferredGoal: Consolidate low-maturity effect/risk synthesis resources into the broader Evidence resource model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep a deprecated R6 core EffectEvidenceSynthesis resource while adding the broader Evidence model.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The inferred goal is reasonable: R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` was trial-use/FMM 0, and R6 `Evidence` now covers variables, statistics, and certainty in one model. A base R6 compatibility resource could have reduced breakage, but it would also perpetuate a separate resource identity for the same evidence facts and complicate APIs, search, validation, and eventual convergence. On the local evidence, the removal is probably justified, though not proven by an official rationale.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` in R6 as a deprecated concrete resource with the R4-compatible shape, while encouraging migration to `Evidence`. That is a real base-design alternative, not merely tooling. It is only a partial alternative because it preserves most R4 instances at the cost of indefinitely supporting two overlapping resource types for effect evidence.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves the old resourceType, but leaves overlapping core resource identities and old low-maturity semantics in place.

evidence.detail: R6 Evidence describes a combined model for variables, statistics, and certainty.
evidence.quote: including the evidence variables ... the statistics, and the certainty

examples.examplesMd: The R4 fragment illustrates the resource identity break: even with required R4 local elements present, the top-level resource type has no R6 core definition. The R6 fragment illustrates why the reverse direction cannot assume every R6 Evidence is an R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis.

findings.narrativeMd: `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` is no longer a core R6 resource. This is the highest-impact change because it happens before any child-element validation: R6 processors do not have a resource definition or generated class for the old resource type. The local evidence suggests the intended target is the broader `Evidence` resource, but that requires a model transform.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: An R4-valid `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` instance can become R6-invalid solely because `resourceType` is unknown in R6 core. The reverse direction is also risky: an R6 `Evidence` instance may express variables or statistics that never corresponded to R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis`. This affects validators, generated SDKs, JSON/XML schemas, FHIRPath paths, subscriptions/search dispatch, and persistence schemas keyed by resource type.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inventory all R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` instances and implement an explicit transform to R6 `Evidence` or a governed compatibility profile. Preserve old `url`, `identifier`, `version`, and citations where possible, then map local evidence variables, statistics, and certainty fields deliberately. Tests should cover strict validation, generated model serialization, API routing, search/indexing, and round-trip data preservation.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The consolidation may be reasonable because the R4 resource was low maturity and overlapped with Evidence/RiskEvidenceSynthesis concepts. A backward-compatible alternative would have been a deprecated R6 resource or formal migration package. That alternative reduces implementation breakage but retains extra resource types and old semantics in the core model.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: A human reviewer should confirm whether ballot change notes explicitly describe the merge into Evidence and whether an official conversion map exists outside the supplied local packages.

findings.title: Mandatory population/exposure/comparator/outcome references were replaced by role-coded Evidence.variableDefinition entries

oldState.summary: R4 required four distinct EvidenceVariable references.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` required `population`, `exposure`, `exposureAlternative`, and `outcome`, each exactly `1..1` and each a `Reference(EvidenceVariable)`. The comparator was encoded structurally as `exposureAlternative`.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence uses repeated variableDefinition entries with a required role code and optional observed/intended references.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Evidence.variableDefinition` is optional and repeatable. Each entry has required `variableRole` and can reference either `Group` or `EvidenceVariable` through `observed` and/or `intended`. Comparator semantics are not a direct old-path rename; they must be represented with variable roles and fields such as `comparatorCategory`.

facts.newValue: No same paths in R6 Evidence
Required variable-role code: population | exposure | outcome | covariate

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The concepts match at a clinical/modeling level, but not at the element-identity level. R4 used fixed element names for population, exposure, comparator, and outcome; R6 uses a normalized list with role codes and separate observed/intended references.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances carry required variable references at paths that R6 `Evidence` does not define. A migration cannot simply change the resource type; it must create multiple `variableDefinition` backbone entries and choose the correct `variableRole`, `observed` versus `intended`, and comparator representation. R6-to-R4 is high risk because R6 supports covariates, `Group` targets, and an observed/intended distinction that R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` cannot represent directly.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Mis-mapping population, intervention/exposure, comparator, or outcome changes the question answered by the evidence and can invert or distort effect interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Normalize evidence variables into a flexible role-coded list that can support more than one evidence design.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain deprecated named population, exposure, exposureAlternative, and outcome fields while adding role-coded variableDefinition.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of a flexible role-coded variable list is reasonable because it supports covariates, Group targets, and observed-versus-intended variables that the old four-field model could not express. Keeping the old named fields in the base model would help R4 data, but it would create two ways to represent the same population/exposure/outcome facts and raise safety-relevant ambiguity when the aliases diverge from `variableDefinition` entries. Those tradeoffs make the breaking redesign probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A less-breaking base R6 design could have kept the R4 named elements as deprecated aliases, perhaps with broader targets and clearer comparator guidance, while also adding `Evidence.variableDefinition`. This would cover the common R4 four-reference pattern but would not cover the full R6 model and would burden validators and implementers with duplicate variable channels and non-trivial consistency checks.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Would preserve common R4 PICO references, but duplicates variable representations and needs consistency rules with observed/intended role-coded entries.

evidence.detail: R4 requires four named EvidenceVariable references.
R6 Evidence defines optional repeated variableDefinition entries.
Each R6 variableDefinition has a required role code.
R6 observed/intended variable references can target Group or EvidenceVariable.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example is illustrative. The exact comparator representation should be confirmed against official R6 guidance or local profiles because R6 no longer has a dedicated `exposureAlternative` path.

findings.narrativeMd: The PICO-like variable model moved from fixed required fields to a normalized list. That affects validation and code because old paths such as `EffectEvidenceSynthesis.exposureAlternative` disappear and business logic must infer roles from `variableDefinition.variableRole` and related fields.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old R4 instances are not valid R6 Evidence because the named fields are absent and the resource identity changed. Even after transformation, validation checks different things: R6 validates a required role code inside each entry, not the existence of four named fields. R6 Evidence can also express covariates or Group-based variables that cannot be round-tripped into R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis without loss or extensions.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Build a deterministic variable mapping. Create at least population, exposure, comparator, and outcome `variableDefinition` entries for each R4 instance; decide whether old references become `observed` or `intended`; and document how `exposureAlternative` maps to comparator semantics. Include test cases with missing optional R6 variables, multiple exposures, Group targets, covariates, and old comparator values.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: The R6 normalized structure is more expressive, so a fully backward-compatible design would have been awkward. Still, a published ConceptMap or compatibility extension/profile could have reduced ambiguity for the common R4 four-field pattern.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Comparator handling is the key ambiguity. The local StructureDefinition exposes `comparatorCategory`, but no official migration rule was present in the supplied inputs.

findings.title: Effect estimates, sample size, precision, and results-by-exposure were remodeled as Evidence.statistic

oldState.summary: R4 used dedicated backbones for sample size, per-exposure risk links, and effect estimates.
oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` had `sampleSize` with integer study/participant counts, `resultsByExposure` with an optional required-bound `exposureState` code and mandatory `riskEvidenceSynthesis` reference when present, and repeatable `effectEstimate` with decimal `value`, required-bound UCUM `unitOfMeasure`, and decimal precision bounds.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence uses repeated statistic entries with Quantity, sampleSize, attributeEstimate, and modelCharacteristic structures.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Evidence.statistic` is the main carrier for effect/risk measurements. It uses `statistic.quantity` rather than separate decimal value plus CodeableConcept unit, nests sample-size counts under `statistic.sampleSize`, represents precision through `statistic.attributeEstimate.quantity` or `.range`, and can add events, affected counts, model characteristics, and nested attributes.

facts.note: R6 count fields reject negative values at the datatype level.

facts.newValue: No same R6 Evidence path; RiskEvidenceSynthesis is listed in R6 old-types

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: The statistical concepts have clear R6 destinations, but the mapping is structural and partly semantic. Point estimates, precision intervals, sample-size counts, and per-exposure risk links do not retain the same paths, datatypes, or target resource identities.

impact.impactRationaleMd: R4 instances using effect estimates or results-by-exposure cannot be accepted by R6 Evidence without transformation. Generated R4 code exposes `effectEstimate.value`, `unitOfMeasure`, `precisionEstimate.from`, and `resultsByExposure.riskEvidenceSynthesis`; generated R6 code exposes `statistic.quantity`, `attributeEstimate.range`, and other statistic structures. R6-to-R4 is high risk because R6 supports richer statistic attributes and model characteristics that have no R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis equivalent.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Effect-size value, units, confidence intervals, sample-size denominators, and per-exposure risks are core clinical/scientific content. Mis-conversion can change the magnitude or interpretation of evidence.

justification.inferredGoal: Replace separate effect/risk-specific estimate backbones with a generalized statistic model.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep deprecated sampleSize, resultsByExposure, and effectEstimate backbones alongside Evidence.statistic.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The generalized R6 `Evidence.statistic` model is a reasonable goal because it can represent point estimates, intervals, event counts, affected counts, and model characteristics in one extensible structure. A compatibility backbone could preserve common R4 content, but it would duplicate the same effect-size facts and leave unclear how old `resultsByExposure.riskEvidenceSynthesis` should work when `RiskEvidenceSynthesis` is also removed. Given those material consistency and safety tradeoffs, the breaking remodel is probably justified.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have retained the old statistical backbones as deprecated fields on a compatibility resource or on `Evidence`, while introducing `Evidence.statistic` for the new model. That would reduce R4-to-R6 data loss for common effect estimates but is incomplete for richer R6 statistics and risks divergent duplicate values for clinically important quantities, units, intervals, and per-exposure risk links.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves many old measurements, but duplicates safety-critical statistics and may require also preserving RiskEvidenceSynthesis.

evidence.detail: R4 defines repeatable effectEstimate backbones with value, unitOfMeasure, and precisionEstimate children.
R4 resultsByExposure requires a RiskEvidenceSynthesis reference when the backbone is present.
R6 Evidence defines repeatable statistic backbones with quantity, sampleSize, attributeEstimate, and modelCharacteristic children.
R6 lists RiskEvidenceSynthesis as an old FHIR type no longer used in this version.

examples.examplesMd: The example shows a likely transformation shape, not an official mapping. Unit conversion from R4 `CodeableConcept` to R6 `Quantity` should be validated carefully.

findings.narrativeMd: R4 effect-synthesis measurements were organized around effect estimates and linked risk syntheses. R6 Evidence instead centralizes measurement data in `statistic`. This is a runtime and semantic migration issue because applications typically calculate, display, and validate these fields directly.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Old `effectEstimate`, `sampleSize`, and `resultsByExposure` elements are not R6 Evidence elements, so old instances fail R6 validation without transformation. The new R6 `unsignedInt` count datatypes also reject negative counts even if an old R4 integer field technically allowed them. R6 statistics with model characteristics, event counts, nested attributes, or non-EffectEvidenceSynthesis variables cannot be faithfully represented in R4 without extensions or data loss.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Create a statistic-mapping table. Map decimal point estimates plus UCUM unit CodeableConcepts into `Quantity`, map precision bounds into `Range`, move sample-size counts under each appropriate statistic, and decide how to replace or preserve `resultsByExposure.riskEvidenceSynthesis` links. Validate clinical displays and calculations after migration, not just JSON shape.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A generalized statistic backbone is more sustainable than separate effect/risk models, but it is not backward compatible. An official StructureMap or compatibility extension set would have reduced implementation risk while allowing the R6 model to move forward.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: The correct destination for `resultsByExposure` may depend on whether separate R4 RiskEvidenceSynthesis instances are also being migrated to R6 Evidence.

findings.title: Certainty ratings changed from repeatable evidence-quality ratings to a narrower Evidence certainty model

oldState.summary: R4 allowed multiple certainty ratings per certainty component.

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: The R4 binding points to the local evidence-quality ValueSet, which includes the terminology.hl7.org evidence-quality CodeSystem. A full code-by-code comparison to the R6 certainty-rating value set could not be completed because the R6 certainty-rating ValueSet was not present as a local core package file.

oldState.narrativeMd: R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis.certainty.rating` was `0..* CodeableConcept` with an extensible binding to evidence-quality. Subcomponents were represented under `certainty.certaintySubcomponent` with their own repeatable ratings.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence has at most one rating per certainty entry and a different terminology family.

binding.description: Assessment or judgement of the aspect

terminologyComparison.terminologyNotesMd: R6 changes both the cardinality and the binding URL/strength. The core package did not include the external terminology value set needed for expansion comparison.

newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Evidence.certainty.rating` is `0..1`, with separate `certainty.type`, `certainty.rater`, and recursive `certainty.subcomponent` structures. The binding uses the external certainty-rating value set at example strength.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: Both paths represent certainty/quality judgments about the evidence. The direct rating path remains recognizable, but its maximum cardinality and terminology binding changed.

impact.impactRationaleMd: An old certainty entry with multiple ratings cannot map one-to-one to a single R6 `Evidence.certainty.rating` because R6 allows only one rating per certainty entry. A transform might split the old ratings into multiple certainty entries or subcomponents, but that is a semantic decision. The binding strength is weaker in R6, which reduces validation hardness but increases terminology migration ambiguity.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Certainty/quality ratings affect how evidence is interpreted and may drive recommendation strength or trust decisions. Combining, splitting, or losing ratings can change downstream interpretation.

justification.inferredGoal: Refactor certainty ratings into a more structured certainty model with typed aspects, raters, and subcomponents.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Keep Evidence.certainty.rating repeatable while adding type, rater, and subcomponent structure.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: The R6 goal of a more structured certainty model is reasonable, but the local evidence does not show why `rating` had to narrow from `0..*` to `0..1`. R6 already permits repeated `certainty` entries and uses an example-strength binding, so retaining repeatable ratings would preserve R4-valid certainty data while still allowing type, rater, and subcomponent modeling. This specific cardinality break therefore looks probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: A base R6 design could have left `Evidence.certainty.rating` at `0..*`, added the new `type`, `rater`, and recursive subcomponent fields, and used definitions or best-practice guidance to prefer one rating per typed aspect. This would preserve most R4 instances without introducing a duplicate element; the main cost is looser normalization and some validation ambiguity for multiple ratings in one certainty entry.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Preserves old multi-rating entries with only moderate ambiguity about whether repeated ratings describe one aspect or several aspects.

evidence.detail: R4 certainty.rating is repeatable and extensibly bound to evidence-quality.
R6 certainty.rating is single-valued and example-bound to certainty-rating.
R6 adds certainty typing and subcomponent structures around the rating.

examples.examplesMd: The migration example splits multiple old ratings into multiple certainty entries. That may or may not preserve intended meaning; a profile-specific rule is preferable.

findings.narrativeMd: The certainty area is not just renamed. R4 allowed multiple ratings within a certainty component and used evidence-quality terminology; R6 uses a more structured Evidence certainty entry with a single rating and different terminology. This can be lossy when old records stored multiple ratings together.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: Because `EffectEvidenceSynthesis` itself is removed, old instances already fail R6 validation. Independently, if the certainty data is migrated to `Evidence`, multiple old ratings cannot occupy one R6 `certainty.rating`. The R6 binding is example strength, so code validity may be less strict, but business rules that expect evidence-quality codes or arrays of ratings can break.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Inspect certainty arrays with more than one rating. Decide whether to split them into multiple `Evidence.certainty` entries, map them to subcomponents, or preserve original structure with extensions. Perform terminology mapping from evidence-quality to certainty-rating where possible and flag unmapped codes for review.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: R6 may be improving semantic precision by separating certainty aspects and ratings, but narrowing cardinality without a formal map is avoidably disruptive for repeatable old ratings.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Terminology confidence is limited because the external R6 certainty-rating value set was not expanded locally.

findings.title: Knowledge-artifact metadata and relationship fields no longer have one-to-one Evidence paths

oldState.summary: R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis exposed definitional metadata fields common to R4 knowledge artifacts.
oldState.narrativeMd: Local R4 fields included `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact`, in addition to canonical metadata such as `url`, `identifier`, `version`, `name`, `title`, `status`, publisher/contact, authorship, and review metadata.

newState.summary: R6 Evidence keeps some canonical metadata but removes or remodels several old local metadata fields.
newState.narrativeMd: R6 `Evidence` has `relatesTo` with typed target choices rather than R4 `relatedArtifact`; it adds fields such as `versionAlgorithm[x]`, `citeAs`, `experimental`, `purpose`, `copyrightLabel`, `assertion`, and `recorder`; and it does not define same paths for `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, or `topic`.

facts.newValue: No same paths on R6 Evidence
relatesTo 0..* BackboneElement with type 1..1 and target[x] 1..1

facts.note: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation tightening, but it creates reverse-conversion requirements.

structuredDelta.matchingRationaleMd: `relatedArtifact` and `relatesTo` are conceptually related but are not the same datatype or content model. Other old fields have no same-path R6 Evidence destination in the supplied StructureDefinition.

impact.impactRationaleMd: Old metadata fields are nested in a removed resource and several have no one-to-one R6 Evidence path. Implementations that use these fields for filtering, jurisdictional applicability, effective dates, topic classification, or citations must choose replacement extensions or profile rules. R6-to-R4 conversion is also not direct because new Evidence metadata and optional status do not fit the old required/status and metadata shape.
impact.safetyOrBusinessRiskMd: Jurisdiction, effective period, and related-artifact metadata can affect which evidence is applicable and which source/citation supports it. Losing this metadata can lead to inappropriate reuse or poor auditability.

justification.inferredGoal: Align Evidence with the R6 canonical/artifact relationship model and remove older knowledge-artifact metadata paths that are not part of the new Evidence shape.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeSummary: Retain optional jurisdiction, effectivePeriod, topic, and relatedArtifact fields on base R6 Evidence while adding relatesTo and newer metadata.
justification.justificationRationaleMd: Aligning `Evidence` with newer metadata and relationship patterns is a reasonable goal, but the removed R4 metadata fields were optional applicability, topic, and citation/relationship carriers. Keeping them as deprecated optional base elements would have preserved most R4 metadata without preventing use of `relatesTo`, `citeAs`, or other R6 fields. Without evidence that these fields would undermine the R6 model, this break appears probably avoidable.
justification.backwardCompatibleAlternativeMd: The best less-breaking base design would have carried forward `jurisdiction`, `effectivePeriod`, `topic`, and `relatedArtifact` on `Evidence`, with clearer definitions and deprecation guidance for cases superseded by `relatesTo` or newer metadata. This is more than a profile or extension workaround and would preserve R4-valid metadata. The tradeoff is that deprecated relationship fields may coexist with `relatesTo` indefinitely, requiring implementation guidance to prevent inconsistent duplicate relationship representations.
justification.alternativeTradeoffSummary: Mostly additive optional fields preserve R4 metadata; the main cost is overlap between relatedArtifact and relatesTo plus a larger Evidence surface.

evidence.detail: R4 defines jurisdiction, effectivePeriod, topic, and relatedArtifact as local EffectEvidenceSynthesis elements.
R6 Evidence uses relatesTo for relationships and does not define same paths for jurisdiction, effectivePeriod, topic, or relatedArtifact.
R6 Evidence status is optional while R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis status was mandatory.

examples.examplesMd: This fragment shows metadata that needs an explicit destination during migration. R6 `relatesTo` may carry some relationship/citation information, but jurisdiction, effectivePeriod, and topic need profile-specific handling if they must be preserved.

findings.narrativeMd: The resource merge also changes the definitional metadata surface. Some old knowledge-artifact metadata fields remain conceptually important but are not available at the same R6 Evidence paths. This is less severe than the statistical and variable remodels, but it matters for systems that index applicability, jurisdiction, and source relationships.
findings.validationAndCompatibilityMd: R4 instances with these fields fail R6 validation under the old resource type and cannot be made valid by simply renaming paths. Some R6 metadata is more permissive or richer, such as optional status and `relatesTo.target[x]`; reverse conversion may require defaulting mandatory R4 status or losing R6-only relationship target forms.
findings.migrationGuidanceMd: Define metadata preservation rules before bulk conversion. Map `relatedArtifact` to `relatesTo` only where type/target semantics are clear, preserve canonical identifiers and citations, and use governed extensions or profiles for jurisdiction/effectivePeriod/topic when required. Rebuild search indexes and filters around the new locations.
findings.backwardCompatibilityAnalysisMd: A broader Evidence metadata model may be appropriate, but removal of common applicability fields without an explicit migration path is disruptive. Compatibility extensions or a StructureMap would have mitigated this without forcing R6 Evidence to retain every old field directly.
findings.reviewerNotesMd: Confirm with the R6 narrative spec whether jurisdiction/effective period/topic were intentionally removed from Evidence or expected to be represented by extensions/profiles.

checkedNoMaterialChange.notesMd: No local EffectEvidenceSynthesis-specific modifier element was identified beyond inherited `implicitRules` and `modifierExtension`, which are out of scope for this artifact report.
No local slicing rules on EffectEvidenceSynthesis were found that need separate migration analysis.
No local fixed value, pattern value, or default value constraints were found for EffectEvidenceSynthesis local elements.

No explicit maxLength, regex, minValue, or maxValue local constraints were found on EffectEvidenceSynthesis numeric fields. R6 datatype changes such as integer to unsignedInt for sample-size counts are covered in the statistic finding.

The local R4 root warning `ees-0` for machine-usable `name` corresponds broadly to the R6 Evidence `cnl-0` warning. This is a codegen/quality warning rather than a hard instance break and is listed as a non-breaking notable change.

`EvidenceVariable` remains an available R6 target through `Evidence.variableDefinition.observed` and `.intended`, but the target domain also adds `Group` and the old `RiskEvidenceSynthesis` reference target is not present as an R6 core resource. Material reference-target issues are covered in findings.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Evidence.status is optional while R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis.status was mandatory
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: This is not an R4-to-R6 validation tightening; old R4 instances already contain `status`. It is still relevant for reverse conversion because a valid R6 Evidence can omit status, while R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis required it.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: When converting R6 Evidence back to an R4-like effect synthesis, choose an explicit policy for missing status rather than silently defaulting to `draft` or `unknown`.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Synthesis and study design metadata became repeatable and use different binding URLs/strengths
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 `synthesisType` and `studyType` were each optional single CodeableConcepts, so increasing repeatability in R6 is not an old-instance validation break after transformation. However, the binding URLs and strength changed, and `studyType` is represented as `studyDesign` in R6 Evidence.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Preserve old codes and text during migration, but review terminology maps from `synthesis-type` and `study-type` to the R6 terminology.hl7.org value sets before using them for decision logic.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: Machine-name warning constraint changed but remains a warning
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: R4 had a local `ees-0` warning that `name` should match a machine-friendly identifier pattern. R6 Evidence has a corresponding `cnl-0` warning with a slightly different expression. Because both are warnings and `name` remains optional, this is primarily a QA/code-generation concern rather than a hard validation break.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: If generated code or artifact publishing pipelines enforce warnings as errors, test short or non-conforming names during conversion.

nonBreakingNotableChanges.title: R6 Evidence adds metadata fields that have no R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis counterpart
nonBreakingNotableChanges.whyNotBreakingMd: Optional R6 additions do not make old R4 data invalid, but they increase R6-to-R4 representability risk because the assigned R4 artifact has no place for some new Evidence metadata.
nonBreakingNotableChanges.migrationAwarenessMd: Forward conversions can leave these fields absent. Reverse conversions should either preserve them in extensions/original-resource sidecars or document that they are dropped.

followUpDependencies.reasonMd: R6 `Evidence` is the likely merge target and should have its own full R4-to-R6 report. That report should own changes to Evidence itself that are not specific to migrating R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis.

R4 `EffectEvidenceSynthesis.resultsByExposure.riskEvidenceSynthesis` referenced `RiskEvidenceSynthesis`, and R6 lists `RiskEvidenceSynthesis` as an old type. Migration of per-exposure results depends on how RiskEvidenceSynthesis is converted.

R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis required references to EvidenceVariable. R6 Evidence variableDefinition still references EvidenceVariable but also allows Group and separates observed/intended variables, so EvidenceVariable changes affect migration fidelity.

followUpDependencies.nameOrUrl: effect-estimate-type, precision-estimate-type, evidence-quality, exposure-state, variable-role, statistic-type, attribute-estimate-type, certainty-rating
followUpDependencies.reasonMd: Terminology maps or expansions are needed to verify how old effect estimate, precision estimate, exposure-state, and certainty codes should map to R6 statistic and certainty terminology.

Inherited Resource/DomainResource and base Element changes, including inherited extension/modifierExtension behavior, are intentionally out of scope here and should be covered by base-artifact reports.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The same-name R6 StructureDefinition is absent. This strongly supports a breaking identity finding but means detailed element comparison relies on the inferred R6 `Evidence` replacement rather than an official one-to-one successor.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: An official R4-to-R6 diff, change note, or migration guide identifying the intended replacement would improve mapping confidence.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: No local ConceptMap or StructureMap was found for R4 EffectEvidenceSynthesis to R6 Evidence. Therefore mapping guidance is inferred from StructureDefinition element semantics and should be reviewed before automated production conversion.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: A published cross-version ConceptMap/StructureMap or HL7 migration note would allow deterministic mapping and clearer lossiness classification.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Terminology expansions were not performed, and several R6 bindings refer to terminology.hl7.org value sets that are not present as local core package files. Code-level removed/added code lists are therefore not complete.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Run terminology expansion/closure for the old and new value sets, then compare codes and displays with any official ConceptMaps.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: The local JSON package proves the structural state but does not include ballot discussion, Jira issues, or narrative rationale for why EffectEvidenceSynthesis and RiskEvidenceSynthesis were removed or merged.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Review the R5/R6 specification narrative, ballot reconciliation notes, and Jira/change proposals for Evidence-Based Medicine resources.

analysisLimitations.descriptionMd: Example JSON fragments in findings are illustrative and focused on the changed fields. They were not run through a full FHIR validator as complete resources with all referenced artifacts present.
analysisLimitations.whatWouldResolveItMd: Create complete R4 and R6 fixture bundles with referenced EvidenceVariable/Group/Evidence resources and validate them with official FHIR validators.
